title: Sweet Osmanthus: Ancient Osmanthus Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A scent tree rarely protected by law. The Kinmokusei of Mishima Taisha, over 1,200 years by tradition, flowers twice every September.
intro: Osmanthus fragrans is grown for one thing: for a few weeks each autumn, a mature tree's small flowers put out one of the strongest scents any hardy plant makes, apricot and ripe peach carried well past the tree itself. It rarely receives official protection of its own, which makes Japan's National Natural Monument osmanthus unusual. The Kinmokusei of Mishima Taisha, over 1,200 years by shrine tradition, flowers twice in the same month, early September and again two weeks later, and a 1985 assessment that gave it three years to live has been wrong for forty. At Eimeiji in Ora a typhoon felled the original in 1966, and the tree there now grew back from its stump. Kezoji's in Maebashi is the child of a famous tree that died. Caserta's, in the royal palace's English Garden, has a 6.5-metre girth made of several stems bundled together.
